title: test-0136-MAT-GRAPHSINTRO
passage: To represent data effectively, we must choose the right type of graph. A bar graph is ideal for comparing categories, where all bars must have equal widths so that only their heights represent the values. In contrast, a line graph is used to show continuous change over time, such as temperature fluctuations throughout a day. When plotting points on a Cartesian plane, we always start counting from the origin, which is the intersection point of the x-axis and y-axis. A coordinate pair like (x, y) tells us the horizontal distance first, followed by the vertical distance. For example, to plot (3, 2), start at the origin, move 3 units to the right along the x-axis, and then 2 units up. When we plot multiple points that follow a linear relationship, we join them with a straight line using a ruler. This line represents all possible points that satisfy the equation, not just the ones we manually plotted. Finally, remember that quadrants are numbered in a counter-clockwise direction, starting from the top right as the first quadrant. Understanding these rules ensures your graphs accurately communicate information without misleading the reader.
